cvStructure.issue: Your CV doesn't have a Skills or Technical Skills section, so recruiters and ATS systems can't quickly see the tools you know in one place.
cvStructure.suggestion: Add a Skills section listing tools you already show elsewhere in your CV, such as Python, TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn, SQL and Power BI.

cvStructure.issue: Your contact details are missing a phone number and a LinkedIn, GitHub or portfolio link, and your email 'nora.alharbi (at) example dot com' is not written in the standard name@domain form.
cvStructure.suggestion: Add a phone number and a link to your LinkedIn or GitHub, and write your email as nora.alharbi@example.com so ATS systems can read it.

sectionOrganization.suggestion: Rename it to 'Experience' so ATS systems recognize the section.

sectionOrganization.issue: The heading 'THINGS I BUILT' is a personal phrase instead of a standard section name.
sectionOrganization.suggestion: Rename it to 'Projects' so ATS systems and recruiters can find this work easily.

sectionOrganization.issue: Your Experience entries are not ordered most recent first: Student Lab Assistant appears before Data Science Trainee and Machine Learning Intern, even though the Machine Learning Intern role, which 'finished in September 2025', ended more recently.
sectionOrganization.suggestion: Reorder them as Machine Learning Intern, then Data Science Trainee (Co-op), then Student Lab Assistant.

keywordUsage.issue: Some tool names are written inconsistently: 'PYTHON' and 'python', 'Tensorflow', 'Pytorch' and 'pytorch', and 'sk-learn' and 'Scikit learn'.
keywordUsage.suggestion: Use the official forms everywhere: Python, TensorFlow, PyTorch and scikit-learn.

keywordUsage.issue: The Arabic Tweets Mood Checker project describes deciding if a writer is happy, angry or neutral, which is sentiment analysis, but that term isn't used anywhere.
keywordUsage.suggestion: Add the term 'sentiment analysis' to this project so recruiters and ATS systems searching for that skill can find it.

keywordUsage.issue: Your graduation project describes telling apart kinds of dates from pictures, which is image classification, but that term isn't used.
keywordUsage.suggestion: Add the term 'image classification' to your graduation project description.

readability.issue: The Data Science Trainee entry is written as one long run-on story covering the whole co-op in a single sentence joined with 'and' and 'so'.
readability.suggestion: Split it into short points, for example one for cleaning delivery data with Pandas, one for predicting late deliveries with scikit-learn, one for building Power BI charts, and one for sharing code with Git.

readability.issue: Several entries are written as first-person stories instead of short points starting with action verbs, including your graduation project and the Arabic Tweets Mood Checker.
readability.suggestion: Rewrite them starting with verbs like 'Built', 'Collected' or 'Trained' instead of 'I made' or 'I gathered'.

readability.issue: Several achievements don't give a specific result, including the late-delivery prediction in Data Science Trainee, the Arabic Tweets Mood Checker, and the House Price Guesser.
readability.suggestion: Add a specific number for each, such as [accuracy percentage] for the late-delivery model and [percentage] for the mood checker.

contentFormatting.issue: The Machine Learning Intern entry lists dates as '2025 - present' but also says the internship 'finished in September 2025', which contradicts an ongoing role.
contentFormatting.suggestion: Change the dates to the actual start and end months, for example 'July 2025 - September 2025', to match the text.

contentFormatting.issue: Dates are written in different formats across your CV, such as '09/2023 - 05/2024', 'March 2025 - June 2025', and just '2025'.
contentFormatting.suggestion: Pick one format, such as 'Month YYYY', and use it consistently for every entry.
